content.text:
The contest is a **two-stage, execution-grounded RAG system**, not a chatbot. You retrieve the right Vietnamese BCTC tables, emit pandas that actually runs, and cite a real source. The write-up of that problem is strong. The remaining risk is calendar: **block E is done; almost everything that scores is not**, and public test closes **31 Aug 2026**.

A structured briefing is in [ViFinQA docs briefing](C:\Users\hahah\.cursor\projects\c-Users-hahah-OneDrive-Documents-code-ai-guru-hkt\canvases\vifinqa-docs-briefing.canvas.tsx) — a live canvas you can open beside the chat.

## What PROBLEM.md is really asking for

The organizer wants a system that, given a Vietnamese financial question:

1. Finds the relevant table(s) (and, separately, text/notes) in ~1,973 OCR reports covering 100 tickers, 2015–2025.
2. Turns the question into **runnable pandas** on those frames.
3. Returns a number that can be checked, with company / year / report / table / page.

Three properties dominate:

- **Retrieval is the ceiling.** Miss the table and perfect code cannot recover.
- **Grounding is required.** Invented cells or citations fail the stated goals even before metrics.
- **The answer is the executed number**, not the model’s prose.

Rules that actually constrain you: **open-weight only, ≤14B, released before 1 Jun 2026**. Closed models are out. A 14B model will not “reason its way” past bad retrieval or dirty schema; you need filter + index + schema in the prompt + an execute–repair loop.

## Scoring: trust PROBLEM.md, treat older boards as folklore

The scoring section in `PROBLEM.md` is now labeled **canonical**. Three automatic, macro-averaged pillars:

| Pillar | Meaning | What it pushes you to do |
|---|---|---|
| **Tables & Docs P/R/F2** (+ MRR@5) | F2 weights **recall ~4× precision**. Both streams are scored. | Take a wider top-k, then rerank. Keep docs “good enough”; do not skip them. |
| **Answer Accuracy** | Number matches gold **within a tolerance that is still unpublished**. | Convert to the unit in the question (`triệu đồng` vs `VNĐ`). |
| **Execution Accuracy** | Pandas **runs and is correct**. | A “just read the table, no code” fallback can save Answer and still **zero Execution**. |

Still unknown: mix of Table vs Doc vs F2 vs Answer vs Execution; whether MRR@5 counts; the numeric tolerance.

Older notes still talk as if **Answer Accuracy ≈ rank** (correlation 0.999) and Docs F2 is saturated. Those Stage-2 snapshot numbers (Answer ~0.24 avg / 0.67 max; Tables F2 ~0.29 / 0.64; Docs F2 ~0.78 / 0.97) are useful as **difficulty**, not as the official formula. `PROBLEM.md` already says the checkpoint used **different column names**.

## What the docs get right

**Opus analysis** (`CLAUDE-OPUS.md`) is the right map: RAG + Text-to-Code + Table QA + Vietnamese financial NLP. The risk chain is correct — bad normalize → silent wrong numbers; missing tables → nothing to compute. Derived ratios (ROE/ROA/growth), unit/period mismatch, parent vs consolidated, and schema hallucination are the real traps.

**Data analysis** is the highest-value file. It corrected the Excel/PDF assumption:

- Tables are **HTML inside OCR `.txt`**, split by `===== PAGE N =====`.
- Filenames already encode **ticker / year / consolidated vs parent**.
- `code_stock.csv` maps ticker ↔ company name.
- **1,012 questions, no answers.** You must hand-label a tiny dev set.
- Questions specify the **output unit**.

That is why metadata filter is not a nicety: it can cut **141k tables down to ~70** in one report.

**Post-data tech review** reorders the stack correctly: metadata first, BM25 earlier than expected (BCTC language is lexical), dense after the filter, rerank cheap on ~70 candidates, **LoRA almost useless without labels**, run 14B as **4-bit AWQ on Kaggle T4**, not on a GPU-less laptop.

**Block E report** shows real progress: **1,973/1,973 files, 141,668 tables, 121,576 text blocks, 0 build errors**, pytest 9/9. VN number parsing, negatives in parentheses, stripping formula junk, and keeping “Mã số” as ID not money — that is the right work.

**Implementation guide, learning path, SemEval-2025 Task 8 / TableLLM pointers** are a competent onboarding pack. SemEval Task 8 is the closest English cousin (pandas + self-debug + open ≤14B).

## Where the docs fight each other (and TODO)

The corpus was written in layers and not fully rewritten when scoring and data landed.

- **“Code is not scored”** is explicitly retracted. Execution Accuracy is live.
- **Project plan** still lists LoRA in phase 3; **tech review** says drop it for round 1.
- **Implementation guide** still mentions `pdfplumber`/`camelot`; the real parser is HTML.
- **TODO.md** still has “run `build_processed` on all 1,973 files” open; the normalize report dated **20 Aug** says that batch **already finished**.
- **Opus vs DeepSeek** analyses largely duplicate. Keep one knowledge map.
- Plan dated from **19 Aug (~12 days)**; today that “first public submit by day 8” is already late.

## The uncomfortable part

With six days to public cutoff, the team has **finished the foundation and not started the contest**. Unchecked: unit convention for answers, 30–50 labeled questions, BM25, dense, RRF, metadata filter, both retrieval evals, prompt/LLM/sandbox/self-correction, end-to-end, submission script.

That is the opposite of the plan’s own rule: **submit a weak full loop early, then iterate on public scores.**

The remaining E items (messy footnote tables, wiring `detect_unit`/`convert` into the answer path) matter, but they are not more important than **one BM25+filter run that produces a file you can submit**.

## What I would actually do

Treat `PROBLEM.md` as spec. Stop growing analyst markdown.

1. **Label ~30 questions** that cover parent vs consolidated, units, multi-year, and a derived ratio. Without this you cannot compare models or retrievers.
2. **Metadata filter + BM25 on `catalog.jsonl`**, then **submit**. That is the cheapest Tables F2 move.
3. **Schema + `df.head` in the prompt, sandbox, 2–3 repair loops, convert units on the way out.** That is both Answer and Execution. No LoRA.
4. Only after a public number: hybrid + rerank, then a **14B AWQ bake-off** (Qwen2.5-Instruct vs Coder vs Qwen3) on Kaggle. Docs: standard hybrid, then stop.

Live sources of truth: **PROBLEM.md**, **data-analysis**, **post-data tech review**, **normalize report**, and a **TODO.md reconciled with those**. Everything else is onboarding.
